title: Lanier High School band and contests
summary: At Lanier High a real music program started; he helped teach and won band contests until disqualified as a professional.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And I had some great teachers, very wonderful people. And later on, after I finished the Ninth Grade, I went to Lanier High School. And they were just beginning to get a school band together. Before then, Professor Harley had taught music in eight schools, so we would see him about fifteen minutes every month, or maybe every other month. So we decided to extend the music program. And Professor Mosely came up from Louisiana, Baton Rouge, Louisiana. He had been teaching at Southern, and he began teaching there. Before then, they only had a choir, of which Miss M.D. Mannen(?) was the choir director.
By the time he got there, I was pretty well advanced, and I was helping him teach the saxophone players and the clarinet players, getting them started in the early stages there.

I had a lot of good moments at (?) high school. From there I played in several band contests throughout the state, and I either won first or second prize on clarinet or saxophones. I ended up always going away with two trophies. That is, until they disqualified me because I was working with the bands around home. They declared me a professional, and so that was the end of my amateur career!
Yeah, I was still in high school. But I was actually out making money. So they disqualified me. But my trophies and everything are still there.
